clean_body: I’ve never felt alone because I have people like you standing with me. | | | | Hi friend, it’s Congresswoman Sarah McBride. Right now, the GOP is using LGBTQ+ people as pawns. They’re not offering solutions to make everyone's lives better. Instead, they’re busy launching attacks — on our rights and yes, on me. As the first openly trans member of Congress, I knew there would be moments like this. But I didn’t run for Congress to debate which bathroom I use or entertain cruelty from my Republican colleagues. I ran to deliver for working families. To fight for paid leave. To protect our freedoms. And I will never stop defending the LGBTQ+ community from attacks, manufactured distractions, and the hostility too many of us endure every day. I won’t let the GOP’s pettiness and bullying derail my work. Has it been easy? No. These fights never are. But I’ve never felt alone — because I have people like you and NV Dems standing with me. Growing up, I couldn’t imagine a future like mine. I wasn’t sure this country’s heart was big enough to love someone like me. Over the last decade, though, I’ve been able to bear witness to change that once seemed so impossible to me as a kid that it was almost incomprehensible. Because people believed it could. Because we fought for it. That’s what Pride means to me. It's a call to action and a reminder that even in the face of hate, we have the power to fight back with love, with truth, and with unshakable resolve. name: Heather Williams, DLCC President
subject: Honoring Speaker Emerita Melissa Hortman
disclaimer_text: paid for by DLCC Victory Fund, 1225 Eye Street NW Suite 1250, Washington, DC 20005
body:
| | |
---
| |
---|---
On Saturday, June 14, we lost a giant in state politics and a beloved DLCC Board member. Speaker Melissa Hortman was the kind of leader everyone deserves – a selfless fighter who never lost sight of what public service was about. It was an honor of a lifetime to know her, learn from her, and call her a friend. Melissa mentored and shaped so many leaders, empowered more people in her community to get involved, and inspired the rest of us to stay in the fight no matter how tough things got. She shared the challenges and sugar-coated nothing. She never lost sight of why this all mattered and worked tirelessly to ensure no one else did either. The wins she delivered for Minnesota families – from paid family medical leave, to protecting reproductive health care, to free school lunches for kids – were hard-fought, and they were done with a humor, humility, and grace that will be irreplaceable in the House chamber. She was a trusted neighbor, a valued friend, and a deeply respected colleague. She was an incredible mother alongside her husband, Mark Hortman. There are no words to express how much our community will miss her leadership and her relentless optimism for everything that her state and our country could be. I hope you’ll join me in honoring Melissa and Mark’s memory by considering the following request from their children, Sophie and Colin.
* Plant a tree.
* Visit a local park and make use of their amenities, especially a bike trail.
* Pet a dog. A golden retriever is ideal, but any will do.
* Tell your loved ones a cheesy dad joke and laugh about it.
* Bake something — bread for Mark or a cake for Melissa, and share it with someone.
* Try a new hobby and enjoy learning something.
* Stand up for what you believe in, especially if that thing is justice and peace.

We are going to miss her presence dearly here at DLCC. – Heather Williams, DLCC President

Friend, we’re sure you’ve been following some of the news around the worsening missile attacks between Israel and Iran.

Thousands of US troops were killed along with hundreds of thousands of Iraqi and Afghan civilians. Both countries were destabilized. ISIS was formed as a direct response. name: Sherrod Brown
subject: Trump is coming for unions
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Dignity of Work PAC
body:
| | |

Friend, imagine waking up tomorrow, getting dressed, drinking your morning coffee, and heading into work only to swipe your badge, see a red light, and learn you'd been fired.

Sounds absurd, right? **But this was the reality for hundreds of federal employees who were affected by Donald Trump and Elon Musk's mass layoffs earlier this year.**
Their union should have been able to protect them – or at the very least been notified of the layoffs and other policy changes. But Trump ignored these requirements and went even farther by issuing an executive order ending collective bargaining rights for most federal workers.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/109764747/552168546/-38565542?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk36-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhY2E1NjJjYi1hOTRiLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RSYeIW6JxvK_CrCNJamGuFTIvrL50T26WQt9wx4dI3I=)
**Make no mistake: Trump is attacking workers' right to unionize because he sees them as a check on his power and the power of his corporate buddies – a check the American people desperately need.**
**I have always supported unions, from federal workers, to teachers, to sanitation workers, to bricklayers, to auto workers – and I always will.[I started the Dignity of Work PAC to elect more leaders who will do the same – and if you believe in this mission, I need you to chip in $5 or more today.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/109764748/552168547/-38565542?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk36-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhY2E1NjJjYi1hOTRiLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RSYeIW6JxvK_CrCNJamGuFTIvrL50T26WQt9wx4dI3I=)**
In the 20th century, the right to bargain collectively revolutionized life for workers in our country, empowering them to fight for better wages, safer working conditions, benefits, and more.

**Today, as workers face stagnant wages, rising costs, and a government that puts billionaires first, we need something just as revolutionary: **a government filled with leaders we can trust, who will truly serve the people they represent, fight for the middle class, and build an economy where workers are the winners.
**I believe this is possible – I wouldn't be in this fight if I didn't. But it's going to take all of us, friend, so I need you with me.[Can I count on you to chip in $5 or more now to join our grassroots movement and help elect leaders across the country who will fight for workers?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/109764749/552168548/-38565542?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk36-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhY2E1NjJjYi1hOTRiLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RSYeIW6JxvK_CrCNJamGuFTIvrL50T26WQt9wx4dI3I=)**

clean_body: | | | Friend, imagine waking up tomorrow, getting dressed, drinking your morning coffee, and heading into work only to swipe your badge, see a red light, and learn you'd been fired. Sounds absurd, right? But this was the reality for hundreds of federal employees who were affected by Donald Trump and Elon Musk's mass layoffs earlier this year. Their union should have been able to protect them – or at the very least been notified of the layoffs and other policy changes. But Trump ignored these requirements and went even farther by issuing an executive order ending collective bargaining rights for most federal workers. = Make no mistake: Trump is attacking workers' right to unionize because he sees them as a check on his power and the power of his corporate buddies – a check the American people desperately need. I have always supported unions, from federal workers, to teachers, to sanitation workers, to bricklayers, to auto workers – and I always will.= In the 20th century, the right to bargain collectively revolutionized life for workers in our country, empowering them to fight for better wages, safer working conditions, benefits, and more. Today, as workers face stagnant wages, rising costs, and a government that puts billionaires first, we need something just as revolutionary: a government filled with leaders we can trust, who will truly serve the people they represent, fight for the middle class, and build an economy where workers are the winners. I believe this is possible – I wouldn't be in this fight if I didn't. But it's going to take all of us, friend, so I need you with me.= If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = In solidarity – always. Peter, You’re likely going to receive a LOT of emails this week, from candidates across the country, asking for money before the end of the quarter deadline. I won’t lie: this is one of those emails! But before I ask, I want to explain why my campaign is _different_ from the rest, and why you should consider contributing today.
1. **The report we’ll file with the FEC will be public information for all to see.** National Republicans and our self-funding opponent will be looking closely for any grassroots weakness they can exploit – and make our lives miserable with hateful ads for the next 18 months. We need a show of strength heading into the summer.

2. **This will be the most competitive House race in Illinois, and one of the closest in the country.** I won his first race by just _four_ points, and it took outperforming the top of the ticket to hold this seat. We need any competitive edge possible in a district this close.

3. **We need trusted leaders, not far-right extremists, representing us in Washington.** As the only meteorologist in Congress, I have decades of built-up trust with the residents of IL-17.

**For those reasons we’re aiming to raise $20,000 between now and the end of the quarter to send a message to the MAGA movement that flipping this seat won’t be easy. ** [**So if you’re able, make a contribution before our FEC deadline, and know I wouldn’t ask if it wasn’t important. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/109765235/552170239/-1472320300?refcode=250617_AbortionBan&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NDI2NiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMWNjZWUyOC1hYjRiLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Sk7TB7qjNIrsHf2MZ9Eax_wEGHjeji-AD_ON9QA7NnY=) Dear friend, In 2023, Ohioans made their voices heard — loudly and clearly. Across rural towns and big cities, across party lines and ideologies, voters came together and chose to **enshrine reproductive rights in our state constitution.** It was one of the most powerful, democratic moments in our state’s history. And now, less than two years later, **Republican lawmakers are trying to erase it.** They’ve introduced legislation that would: 🔴 Ban abortion, with **criminal penalties and even homicide charges**
🔴 Threaten access to IVF and other fertility treatments
🔴 Restrict forms of contraception that Ohioans depend on Let’s call this what it is: **an outrageous attempt to override the will of the people.** It’s clear that some politicians didn’t like the outcome of the election — so now they’re trying to go around the voters entirely. That’s not just wrong. It’s dangerous. As the **Democratic Leader of the Ohio House** , I’m leading the charge to stop these attacks. Our caucus is united in putting **people over politics** — and protecting the reproductive freedom that Ohioans already voted to guarantee. We are standing up for our democracy, for the rule of law, and for every family who deserves the freedom to make decisions about their own bodies and futures without government interference. But we need your help to keep up this fight. subject: broken

body:
Do you ever see headlines like these and wonder, “how did our politics get so broken?”
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=2657%2E400544%2EnPcDrc)
Do you ever see headlines like these and wonder, “how did our politics get so broken?”
[
](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250617_1_poor?amount=5&refcode=em20250617-2657&refcode2=2657_400544_nPcDrc&akid=2657%2E400544%2EnPcDrc)_It’s like Robin Hood, but in reverse. They’re stealing from the poor to hand permanent tax cuts to mega-millionaires._
I’ll tell you something I learned about MAGA Republicans who are calling the shots in D.C.:
Most of them can’t begin to relate to the lives of working New Mexicans.
Most of them haven’t ever had to do mental math in line at the grocery store, frantically calculating whether your SNAP benefits will stretch far enough.
Most of them don’t know how it feels to watch overdraft fees pile up while praying that your paycheck will hit in time to pay rent.
Most will never understand how expensive it is to be poor.
My path to public service has been anything but conventional. When I was a single mom just trying to make ends meet for Somáh and me, I probably would’ve laughed if you told me I’d be running for governor of New Mexico one day.
**But these are the life experiences and struggles that made me fierce.** And they’re why I’m so determined to deliver bold solutions that alleviate the poverty, homelessness, and food insecurity weighing heavy on our state. Winning this race won’t be easy, but I’m hopeful that, by working together, we can enact smart, compassionate policies that make life a little easier for hardworking families.
[**If your budget allows, will you make a $5 contribution to our campaign today? Even a small amount would go a long way in our fight.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250617_1_poor?amount=5&refcode=em20250617-2657&refcode2=2657_400544_nPcDrc&akid=2657%2E400544%2EnPcDrc)
**[Donate $5 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250617_1_poor?amount=5&refcode=em20250617-2657&refcode2=2657_400544_nPcDrc&akid=2657%2E400544%2EnPcDrc)**
When I say I want to change the game for New Mexico, here’s what I mean:
* Tackling the housing and affordability crisis that’s holding families back
* Creating high-paying jobs and making it easier to start and run a small business
* Investing in quality public schools so our kids can get a good education
* Protecting our lands and building a sustainable, resilient climate future
* Making sure no one in our state goes hungry because they can’t afford groceries

It’s clear to everyone but the billionaires that our current system isn’t working. So it’s time to choose a new path, where working people’s voices aren’t drowned out by corporate lobbyists and greedy special interests.
**That’s why I’m relying on generous contributions from you and this grassroots team.**
[**If you can pitch in $5 to our campaign right now, it’d go a long way in showing that lobbyists and corporations won’t run New Mexico – we do.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_dh_20250617_1_poor?amount=5&refcode=em20250617-2657&refcode2=2657_400544_nPcDrc&akid=2657%2E400544%2EnPcDrc)
Be fierce,
Deb

name: Dr. Annie Andrews
subject: Spineless Lindsey Graham
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24-annieandrews?refcode=250617em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24-annieandrews?refcode=250617em]
I’m Dr. Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, a mom of three, and the Democrat running for U.S. Senate to defeat Republican Lindsey Graham in South Carolina.
If we flip this seat, we can end Lindsey Graham’s career and help Democrats retake the Senate, and expand the map for Democrats in future elections
I know this won’t be easy. But I’ve treated kids who were shot, hospitalized, and failed by broken systems. Nothing about this moment feels optional.
We need an overwhelming surge of grassroots support in these early days to prove that we can finally defeat Lindsey Graham. So I’m humbly asking: Will you chip in a split donation of $50, $25, or even a $3 donation between Tobias Read and my campaign before midnight to become a Founding Donor of my campaign? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24-annieandrews?refcode=250617em]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24-annieandrews?refcode=250617em]
Let me introduce myself.
I’ve spent nearly 20 years serving my community as a pediatrician, treating everything from asthma and violent trauma to the emotional toll of growing up in poverty.
I’ve seen what bad policy does to good families — and I’ve seen kids suffer because people like Lindsey Graham would rather protect their own power than protect children.
In 2022, after 15 years of working in hospitals, I ran for Congress because I knew our kids needed a voice in Washington. I lost — and I told my oldest daughter I wouldn’t run again.
But then Trump’s chaos came back.
And Lindsey Graham? He cheered.
The truth is, I’m scared. And I’m angry. And I’m done waiting.
So I’m stepping up — because our kids, and this country, can’t afford another six years of Lindsey Graham.
I’m building a people-powered campaign to flip South Carolina and give kids the voice they deserve. And I need your help. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24-annieandrews?refcode=250617em]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24-annieandrews?refcode=250617em]
Thank you — from the bottom of my heart. This campaign is for the kids, but it only works with you in it.
Until the kids are alright,
Dr. Annie Andrews

Dear Friend,I think you agree that we used to be a nation where most everyone loved our national motto, “IN GOD WE TRUST.” After all, Judeo-Christian values guided us to become a great nation – a beacon of God’s goodness. But we have to face the disheartening reality that the agenda pushing harmful ideas like CRT and gender fluidity have led many away from God – maybe even people you know and love. And that’s never more obvious than this month of June when the Left “celebrates” Pride Month.
---
* Men dressed as women swarm libraries for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where they groom small children with books like: “The Hips on the Drag Queen Go Swish, Swish, Swish.”
* Retailers break out their rainbow flags and slogans
* And anyone who dares to disagree with them is shouted down and called a “bigot,” or a “transphobe,” or a “fake Christian.”

---
| | Friend, BRAVE Books is the antidote to this radical ideology. Thanks to patriots like you, we’re instilling conservative values in children using high-quality, wholesome, and Godly books and entertainment. And I’ve never been more grateful. Right now, “IN GOD WE TRUST” is weighing heavily on my mind. Because when I look at what we’re facing, I know He is where my strength lies. And I’m writing you today because you deserve to know where things stand. Our launch of our children’s show “Iggy and Mr. Kirk” was a smash, our 17-citty church tour with Kirk Cameron reached thousands of families, our beautiful Easter allegory “Saving the Easter Bunny” was loved by families... ...AND we launched our very own family-focused streaming service called BRAVE+ to be a foil for woke Disney+ and Netflix! But – we can’t stop now. If we’re going to turn back the Left and truly stop them from filling our children’s hearts and minds with filth... ... we have to do it NOW while we have momentum on our side. In stark contrast to the Left’s “Drag Queen Story Hours,” we pledge allegiance to the flag, pray, and read wholesome books together like Kirk’s BRAVE Book, “Pride Comes Before the Fall.” In “Pride Comes Before the Fall” we teach children that pride is a sin – not something to be celebrated! In the past, other BRAVE Books’ authors like Riley Gaines and Missy Robertson have joined us for “See You at the Library Day” and I’m eager to get the final list together of this year’s authors and share it with you. | Over the weekend, I was informed that my name appeared on a list found in the vehicle of the man who shot and killed former Minnesota House Speaker Melissa Hortman and her husband, and wounded Senator John Hoffman and his wife.

Several other public officials were also on his list because of the values we stand for.

First and foremost, my heart is with the families grieving the loss of Melissa Hortman and her husband, and with Senator Hoffman and his wife as they recover.

**This act of violence was horrifying and deeply personal to all of us who believe in public service. The Hortmans were people who dedicated their lives to their communities. They should still be with us.**

Let me be very clear: Political violence has no place in our country. It is an attack on our democracy itself, and we cannot allow it to be normalized or ignored.

Out of an abundance of caution, my team and I made the difficult decision to postpone our planned town hall in Muskegon yesterday. That decision was about protecting public safety and law enforcement resources, not about backing down. **Because I am not backing down.** I will continue to serve West Michigan. I am steadfast in my commitment to fight for the values that brought me to Congress.

But this moment isn’t just about one district or one voice. It’s about whether we allow extremists to scare us into silence, or whether we rise up and organize to take back the House and put power back in the hands of the people.

Michigan is the tipping point. And holding this seat is essential to flipping the majority. We cannot allow threats to derail the urgent work ahead. There’s too much at stake.

# Melton for Iowa 2026
---
---
| Hello Peter,

This was one of the toughest decisions I've ever had to make, but I know after a lot of prayer, conversation, and thought that I need to suspend my campaign at this time.
It's been one of the tougher past few weeks of my life. I was notified due to reorganization at the company I've long worked for that I'm losing my job, and as the sole breadwinner at home, I really need to find a new job to support my family. I am also now dealing with a health concern I need to prioritize. Additionally, through a month of campaigning, it is clear my 6 year old son at home is finding it much harder to have me on the road, and that of course makes it harder on my wife as well, and both have already sacrificed so much during my first two runs.
It was an honor to fight the good fight on your behalf, and I will continue to, just in different ways. It's the biggest sacrifice I've ever made for the greater good, but I don't regret a single minute, and am proud of the fact that the party out here in the 4th is in a much better place now than it was when I first began running. It was an honor to help party build at the county level and to boost our candidate count last cycle.
I am proud of the work we've done fighting against eminent domain abuse across the partisan divide, the cancer crisis, corporate money and corruption in politics, and water pollution. I'm also proud that I received the unprecedented endorsement of Rep. Feenstra's Republican primary challenger last campaign, sending the Iowa GOP leadership into a week of panic posting on social media, showing they clearly don't think their hold on this state is as guaranteed as they want us to believe. I know in my heart they can't just keep taking their rank and file for granted. It will eventually catch up with them.
I'm also contented that so many first time candidates have reached out to me for advice and have thanked me for opening the door for progressive candidates to run in this state. I'll be rooting for all of them however I can.
I'm also fulfilled that we improved our vote share in our second campaign in 33 of the 4th's 36 counties while staying steady in the other 3 in a down cycle for Democrats nationally, without taking a single penny of corporate PAC money and while working a full time job while raising a family, while also receiving no help or acknowledgment from the national party.
The final thing I want to mention is running for office is much more accessible and doable for people who don't come from wealth and aren't anointed or recruited by anyone than you might think. I showed you can cause a lot of good trouble through a grassroots campaign. I started from literally nothing my first campaign. I wasn't recruited by anyone, had no start up money, and had no name recognition. This was never something I thought I'd do with my life, but when it was clear our party wasn't going to be able to find a candidate, I jumped in and learned on the fly, and so many awesome volunteers boosted us. We need more working people that struggle every day along with most Americans to run for every office, and I'll always make time for you if you want to call me to inquire. Also, even if you are in a district that may seem unwinnable on Election Day, run anyway, because if you tell the truth and run as a sacrifice for the greater good, you'll find so many wins out there.
Thank you so much friends, and I'm so sorry I have to do this. I'll be around, and maybe I'll see you at the next protest. Peace to you all, Ryan Melton

Feenstra's Republican primary challenger last campaign, sending the Iowa GOP leadership into a week of panic posting on social media, showing they clearly don't think their hold on this state is as guaranteed as they want us to believe. I know in my heart they can't just keep taking their rank and file for granted. It will eventually catch up with them. I'm also contented that so many first time candidates have reached out to me for advice and have thanked me for opening the door for progressive candidates to run in this state. I'll be rooting for all of them however I can. I'm also fulfilled that we improved our vote share in our second campaign in 33 of the 4th's 36 counties while staying steady in the other 3 in a down cycle for Democrats nationally, without taking a single penny of corporate PAC money and while working a full time job while raising a family, while also receiving no help or acknowledgment from the national party. The final thing I want to mention is running for office is much more accessible and doable for people who don't come from wealth and aren't anointed or recruited by anyone than you might think. I showed you can cause a lot of good trouble through a grassroots campaign. I started from literally nothing my first campaign. I wasn't recruited by anyone, had no start up money, and had no name recognition. This was never something I thought I'd do with my life, but when it was clear our party wasn't going to be able to find a candidate, I jumped in and learned on the fly, and so many awesome volunteers boosted us. We need more working people that struggle every day along with most Americans to run for every office, and I'll always make time for you if you want to call me to inquire. Also, even if you are in a district that may seem unwinnable on Election Day, run anyway, because if you tell the truth and run as a sacrifice for the greater good, you'll find so many wins out there. Thank you so much friends, and I'm so sorry I have to do this. I'll be around, and maybe I'll see you at the next protest. Peace to you all, Ryan Melton | | | | | | | | | == | == == == | == | P.O. A memorial honors slain Minnesota State Representative Melissa Hortman and her husband, following their assassination in a politically motivated shooting. (Photo via PBS / AP)
It used to be shocking.
My congressional classmate [Gabby Giffords](https://substack.com/redirect/95fe14bc-0b4b-43d0-8afd-ed07cffa81a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was shot at a constituent event in 2011. In 2014, a [Molotov cocktail was tossed through a Congressman's window](https://substack.com/redirect/f46c0f8c-eebb-489a-b969-53681b880c91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). [Pipe bombs](https://substack.com/redirect/595f1806-1af2-4709-910f-0b054bd5cc5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) were mailed to CNN in 2021. Two assassination attempts were made on President Trump during his campaign. And who can forget the Capitol insurrection on January 6? Then there's this past weekend, in Minnesota, where [State Representative Melissa Hortman and her husband were assassinated](https://substack.com/redirect/67aa7c87-e3ec-4675-a039-4755358b77dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [Senator John Hoffman and his wife were shot](https://substack.com/redirect/6c4bdc8f-07af-4b63-bded-c2e3d76ead3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and nearly killed by a man wearing a fake police uniform and carrying a kill list of 45 public officials.
Today, political violence is no longer shocking. It's expected.
This phenomenon was perfectly captured by _[The New York Times](https://substack.com/redirect/b9c35240-77b5-4467-8153-97d4ba811019?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) _reporter Lisa Lerer _:_
> The statements of shock and condolences streamed in eerily one after another on Saturday after the assassination of a Minnesota lawmaker and her husband, and the attempted murder of another lawmaker and his wife.
> "Horrible news," said Representative Steve Scalise, who was shot at a baseball game in 2017. "Paul and I are heartbroken," said former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, whose husband was bludgeoned with a hammer in 2022. "My family and I know the horror of a targeted shooting all too well," said former Representative Gabby Giffords, who was shot in the head in 2011.
> Still more came from Gov. Josh Shapiro of Pennsylvania (arson, 2025), Gov. Gretchen Whitmer of Michigan (kidnapping plot, 2020) and President Trump (two assassination attempts, 2024).
Violence today isn't just tolerated by the shadowy political extremes anymore. It's being[ justified](https://substack.com/redirect/6b21944d-b249-4a5a-a2b1-7de7c20978f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [memed](https://substack.com/redirect/59d1886f-caf3-43fa-9170-dda0794b744d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), rationalized, and even celebrated publicly. What was once the hidden fringe is now cloaked in the language of justice and ["resistance by any means necessary."](https://substack.com/redirect/caec7587-4f98-4a61-89dd-5aebaba62a1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We are witnessing the mainstreaming of murder as we saw with the [internet's glorification of Luigi Mangione.](https://substack.com/redirect/f1e42553-c10a-4c9f-9e33-5b4e32c43ec9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The man who killed UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson is publicly celebrated with t-shirts of his handsome face and now, a [sold-out musical](https://substack.com/redirect/475c06c5-97b1-4144-9b00-f614e429114c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in San Francisco. What type of message are we sending when political violence is treated as virtuous?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/70d7ff2e-0df9-4559-93ff-7d51378ec91d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Luigi Mangione, (Photo via ABC News)
Over the past year, America has seen a surge in political violence so frequent, so ideologically twisted, and so brazen, that it's hard to keep track. What was once fringe behavior has crept into the mainstream. It's no longer coming from the shadows. It's on social media.
## **Enter Hasan Piker**
With over[ 4.5 million followers on Twitch and YouTube](https://substack.com/redirect/0601344b-e740-476b-ab2e-4a05330c95f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and another 1.3 million on [Instagram](https://substack.com/redirect/79b39782-820d-4007-9e9b-350ffd7abb4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Hasan Piker is one of the most influential political streamers in the country--arguably the left's most viral voice. But beneath the Gen Z swagger and thirst traps lies a deeply troubling pattern.
He has said ["America deserved 9/11,"](https://substack.com/redirect/02757e6b-f917-426a-97ba-e7904f83bbf9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) described Jewish victims of October 7th as spreading ["rape fantasies,"](https://substack.com/redirect/02757e6b-f917-426a-97ba-e7904f83bbf9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and downplayed Hamas's atrocities as "resistance." He has publicly declared he has "no issue" with Hezbollah, a U.S.-designated terrorist organization, and gave a platform to a member of the Houthis--another U.S.-designated terror group.
All this has been documented in [Congressman Ritchie Torres' formal letter to Twitch and Amazon ](https://substack.com/redirect/02757e6b-f917-426a-97ba-e7904f83bbf9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)executives condemning Piker.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ba04247e-c0d8-4e22-9434-f08559c773eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Twitch streamer Hasan Piker in his Los Angeles home studio on Aug. 15. Brock Stoneham / NBC News file
We've reached a point where people don't just want to win the argument. They want to punish the other side in ways that are, at best, dehumanizing and grotesque, and at worst, incite violence.
If we don't make a collective effort to change the culture, we surrender to a new normal in which violence replaces debate as another political tool.
### **American Jews Have Become a Target For Violence**
Just this past month, [Sarah Milgrim and Yaron Lischinsky were murdered ](https://substack.com/redirect/a9e8fb2d-8180-4330-a2f8-fffb0b5db4be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)in broad daylight outside the Capital Jewish Museum in D.C. Why? Because they attended an event hosted by the American Jewish Committee. It didn't matter that their program was on providing humanitarian aid to Gaza and seeking interfaith solutions. Their killer was hailed online as a "freedom fighter" by some of the staunchest anti-Israel advocates.
About a week later, in Colorado, a group of Jews calling for the release of Israeli hostages was [firebombed with Molotov cocktails.](https://substack.com/redirect/4729cb15-73a5-44fa-ab68-2a6de7ee2d22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A few months earlier, during Passover, [Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro's residence was set on fire ](https://substack.com/redirect/64895284-0deb-4845-84e0-fa3f3d439042?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)while his family slept inside.
Each of these attackers claimed they did it for Gaza. In case there was any confusion on whether attacking random Jews will make lives better for Palestinans, the answer is a resounding no. That hasn't stopped conspiracy theories from taking aim at Jewish communities, though. The ADL cites a [360% increase in antisemitic incidents](https://substack.com/redirect/e42c32f1-a165-4616-b842-70622a0debd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) since the start of the October 7th Hamas massacre of Israelis.
None of this is activism. It's domestic terrorism.
Sadly, yet unsurprisingly, the deaths of Sarah Milgrim and Yaron Lischinsky were not met with universal condemnation.
Instead, swaths of the anti-Zionist activist world responded with glee and justification. One far-left group, _Unity of Fields_ , distributed a printable zine praising the killer. Stickers were made. TikToks posted. Influencers with millions of followers defended the murders as "resistance."
The [Anti-Defamation League](https://substack.com/redirect/55e9cca7-bc10-4a9c-8697-7dd2eaf2caf9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) documented it all in a new report. "_We ain 't condemning shit,_" one group posted. Another wrote, "_What Elias Rodriguez did is the highest expression of anti-Zionism._ "
The ADL report documented another incident where a DSA-affiliated caucus--the so-called "Liberation Caucus"--endorsed these sentiments, quoting Maoist slogans about rebelling against "the enemy" and reposting images glorifying the killer. The DSA's national office later issued a short, vague disavowal, but only after public pressure mounted.
## **A Shared Delusion**
We've built entire online ecosystems around this. Ragebait headlines. Viral videos calling people "Nazis" or "terrorists" for voting a certain way. T-shirts that say "Kill Your Local Fascist." AI-generated media meant to fan the flames of hatred.
It's all a joke. Until it isn't.
Ask yourself:
Have you ever self-censored online, not because you feared backlash, but because you feared violence?
Have you felt that the angriest, most hateful voices are the ones running the show?
You're not imagining things.
This is the world we've built by rewarding rage with relevance.
And unless we reverse course, it's only going to get worse.
### **This Shouldn 't Be a Partisan Issue**
You don't need to be a Democrat to condemn arson. You don't need to be a Republican to denounce assassination. You just need to be a decent human being and have a smidge of political courage.
We don't have to vote the same to agree that:
Murder is not a political tactic.
[Firebombing a Tesla dealership](https://substack.com/redirect/0367bd10-3bd6-4652-afa5-a6aa0cd9ac18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is not making a domestic policy argument.
[Impersonating a cop to assassinate a state representative ](https://substack.com/redirect/08a14cc3-9724-468c-a1d3-9aa1b135123d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)is not activism--it's terrorism.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/24574b11-f691-47b5-b968-8b38a3e88036?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Spotted in Sunnyside, NY.
If you've ever scanned a crowd at a protest wondering if someone brought a gun, you sadly know this feeling.
Sadly, I do too.
In 2010, after casting my vote in favor of the Affordable Care Act, I started receiving death threats.
I'd come home to Bucks County, worried about the safety of my kids, Maggie, who was 4, and Jack, just 1.
At the time, I was one of the least wealthy members of Congress; I'm still paying off my student loans. Every night in DC, I slept on an inflatable mattress in my office.
One night, after saying goodnight to my kids from the phone, I was startled awake by back-to-back-to back phone calls from a number I didn't recognize. When I finally answered, all I heard was _" Is this Patrick Murphy?!? You're dead when you come back to Bucks County. Do you hear me?!? You're dead when you come back to Bucks County!"_
Being a former Army paratrooper, I couldn't help but to answer, "Who the fuck is this?"
Believe it or not, he actually shared his name. So, I made it clear, "If you ever call me again, I'm coming to your house and I'm going to break your face! Have fun talking to the FBI, that's my next call!"
Then I hung up and called the Capitol Police.
And if you're starting to feel like this country is being held hostage by the loudest, most hateful people in the room, you're not alone.
The left isn't all extremists. The right isn't all fascists. But the volume knob is broken.
## **How we fix our broken culture**
This is beyond politics. This is a cultural problem. Which means it requires a cultural fix.
Talk to someone you disagree with, and actually listen.
Demand better from your party. Yes, yours.
Vote with your values, not your vengeance.
We are still a country that chooses its leaders with ballots, not bullets. But that only holds if we insist on it.
Spirited debate is what separates us from other countries that limit freedom of speech.
Politics will always be messy. But it should never be lethal.

We are living in crazy times. But God ordained each and every one of us for this season and for His reason. And as things seem to get crazier by the day, I want to share a Biblical perspective on this hour we’re in. And in this hour, some of the key characters in the Book of Revelation are on center stage, engaging in an ever-escalating conflict. Israel, God’s chosen people, and Iran—Persia in Biblical times—are at war. Israel has been in God’s plan for the redemption of the world from the very beginning, and those who hasten the destruction of Israel are fighting a losing battle against God Himself. Yet in the midst of this, we must remember and pray for the hundreds of thousands of believers in Iran.

Because of the increase of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold. But the one who stands firm to the end will be saved. And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.”— Matthew 24:10–14 What a great promise. The Great Commission will be fulfilled. There’s no army, force, nuke, or missile strong enough to undo the prophetic promise of Matthew 24:14. Although things get crazy in the end, the Great Commission will still happen. Every nation, tribe, and tongue will hear the gospel. But what is our role as believers? How do we respond? clean_body: | | | | | Dear Peter, We are living in crazy times. But God ordained each and every one of us for this season and for His reason. And as things seem to get crazier by the day, I want to share a Biblical perspective on this hour we’re in. And in this hour, some of the key characters in the Book of Revelation are on center stage, engaging in an ever-escalating conflict. Israel, God’s chosen people, and Iran—Persia in Biblical times—are at war. Israel has been in God’s plan for the redemption of the world from the very beginning, and those who hasten the destruction of Israel are fighting a losing battle against God Himself. Yet in the midst of this, we must remember and pray for the hundreds of thousands of believers in Iran. | | | | So how do we pray? Matthew 24 has good insight: “At that time many will turn away from the faith and will betray and hate each other, and many false prophets will appear and deceive many people. Because of the increase of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold. But the one who stands firm to the end will be saved. And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.”— Matthew 24:10–14 What a great promise. The Great Commission will be fulfilled. There’s no army, force, nuke, or missile strong enough to undo the prophetic promise of Matthew 24:14. Although things get crazy in the end, the Great Commission will still happen. Every nation, tribe, and tongue will hear the gospel. But what is our role as believers? How do we respond? We pray.We get in the Word.We worship.We live our lives with joy in the midst of it all. body:
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/109769046/552183334/-1591572682?refcode=250617_MFC_Annie_Racing&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZDVmYTI2NS1iNTRiLWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=yidyNC5Iso3mue3_ZV853DmV_Mk1D806JC4X7ohn8vc=) Friend, Growing up with two brothers, I had a fierce competitive streak. It was a big week at Forward - here's what you missed.

| | [ ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=JgyyvCfQwldlSeD7KJl_Ih7269o_4hwqOhPs1_PHvgI&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_69&n=1)

Tuesday, June 17, 2025 | Peter -- Before we dive in today, we're making a slight change. Over the past few months, we've been coming to you each week asking your thoughts on all the biggest issues facing America and calling it _**Controlling What You Can.**_ Today, we're officially rebranding this initiative. Instead of focusing on presenting changes that we think are achievable, we instead want to think about the future where America continues to grow and become the best version of itself. We think of democracy as a verb, and that means everyone who loves America needs to work to improve it. As we think about this positive vision for America, we're going to keep asking ourselves some key questions. How can we improve our our communities? How can we build better lives for ourselves? What do we owe to each other (our families, neighbors, communities, country)? How can we plan for the unforeseen? How can we build a just, fair, and honest government that represents Americans? It's going to take _**Forward Thinking**_ __ from us all, so that's the new name of this collaboration with each of you. Welcome to it: let's get thinking! Back to the topic at hand, this week, we asked you about Social Security reforms. Looking at the results, two things stick out to us. First, the top two answers both reflect a general desire to focus the program on helping low-income individuals. The program was designed to help keep America's elderly out of poverty, and it has an outsized effect at lower incomes. 80% of you believed that the tax cap should be eliminated, and benefits should be reduced or eliminated for the wealthy, suggesting that you think those at the top end of the income distribution should pay more into it, while benefits should primarily go to those who need them in retirement. This is reinforced by the relatively low selection of increasing the SS tax rate across the board, reflecting that most of you believe it's only those at the top of the tax bracket who should be contributing more. Second, there was more than a baseline level of support for raising the retirement age. We'll dig more into notes around that below, in our summary of the responses. Social Security reform is complex, and so there were many comments left to dive into more detail: **Privatization and Opt-Out Proposals**
* Many highlighted that their main issue with the program is that it's managed by the government. A significant segment of the responses suggested that money paid into the system be put into private retirement accounts.
* Others called for an opt-out process, allowing individuals to leave the system altogether. This would decrease the inflow of cash to fund it while also decreasing the amount of money that would need to be paid out.

**Raising the Retirement Age**
* For those that selected raising the retirement age, it was noted that we have a longer healthy life expectancy than we did when the program was created. Raising the retirement age, you argued, would have people contribute longer and withdraw for less time, thus alleviating some of the financial pressure on the system.

**Replace Social Security with Something** **Else**
* Some of you even called for the end of the program, shifting the resources to something such as a UBI or a flat pension for everyone. That's certainly ambitious!

And we're the least well known. The race for Governor in New Jersey will hinge on independents, and Forward CEO Lindsey Drath provides some key insights about them. **[FWD CEO Lindsey Williams Drath Joins Chuck Todd on The Toddcast](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=_KeSraPW0gSlxEBMOvJrEouH4SjeZmYtvTWulgNFAfbVxsFlevpWCYVQEYWPLV5F&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_69&n=3)** | **The Chuck Toddcast** Lindsey joins Chuck Todd to discuss all things Forward in an hour-long call about the Party. They talk about what it means to be Forward and how the party will grow in the coming years.
**June 17 | A Juneteenth Conversation With Speaker Terrance Carroll
** Join us for ** _A Juneteenth Conversation with Speaker Carroll_** , a powerful virtual gathering hosted by the **Forward Party’s Black Voters Committee** , honoring the history of Juneteenth and exploring the future of Black leadership and civic power in America. **[Register →](https://home.forwardparty.com/bvc_juneteenth?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_69&n=4)** **June 17 | NOVA FWD Social
** Meet up with NOVA Forwardists for food, drinks, & conversation at a fun location in Fairfax County. Bring your questions, ambitions, and thirst! Why not grab a few friends to come with you, too? **[Register →](https://home.forwardparty.com/nova_fwd_social_20250617?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_69&n=5)** **June 21 | Young Forwardists Chapter Meeting
** Join the Young Forwardists team**at 7:00 PM EST/4:00 PM PST** for our Chapter Information Meeting! Chapters are the backbone of the Young Forwardists. As our political divisions continue to grow, it's up to every student at every high school and college to lead the charge toward change! **[Register →](https://home.forwardparty.com/chapter_information_meeting_20250621?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_69&n=6)** **June 23 | BVC Events Committee Meeting

I must say - this one stings, Fellow Patriot...
I woke up to the unfortunate news that we came up short of our May end-of-month goal. We were on pace until the very last 48-72 hours, then fundraising dropped off a cliff in the final sprint.
I'm disappointed. Not in you (never in you) but in myself.
Whether I didn't explain the urgency well enough or my emails were missed, regardless, we failed. And it hurts.
Why? Because the Democrats are already circling my race like sharks.
\- They named me as their ONLY House Republican target in all of Texas \- TX-15 is one of just THREE seats they need to take back the House
\- If they win here, they'll impeach Trump and block his entire agenda

name: Ruben Gallego
subject: We’ve got to defend our public lands right now
body:
We all lose millions of acres of land that was entrusted to us by previous generations. Our children and our grandchildren lose access to those lands for good. Veterans lose a critical resource in dealing with their PTSD.
#

Can’t even believe I’m writing this, Peter, but the GOP is figuring out ways to make this budget they’re trying to force down our throats even worse.
Senator Mike Lee, while he wasn’t too busy tweeting conspiracies about a politically motivated assassination in Minnesota, just rolled out a plan to sell off millions of acres of protected federal lands as part of this massive tax break bill.
We’re talking about Forest Service, Bureau of Land Management, masses of lands in Alaska, Arizona, Utah, the pacific northwest, and more. This would be a land grab the likes of which we have never seen in our lifetimes.
Who wins here? Billionaires who want to build mansions on land we all cherish.
Who loses? Basically everybody else.
Seriously. We all lose millions of acres of land that was entrusted to us by previous generations. Our children and our grandchildren lose access to those lands for good. Veterans lose a critical resource in dealing with their PTSD
And for what — to lower the price tag of trillions of dollars in tax breaks for the wealthiest people in the country? Hell no. Nobody wants this.
This has to stop, and I’m asking you for your help.
[**Please, add your name and join me in defending our public lands. We’ve got to hold the line and make some noise here.** [ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/250617_pet_em_public_lands/?source=em250617-1-160+&akid=3893%2E734936%2EmT3QkW) Thank you, Ruben

body:
The Trump administration is coming up with a lot of ways to attack our voting rights. | |

Peter, **One of the most effective ways to attack a democracy? By making it harder for people to make their voices heard.** It’s bad enough that our aging voting infrastructure is facing increasing cyberattacks, our election workers are dealing with threats and harassment, and voters are wading through a sea of disinformation and AI. Now, the Trump administration is coming up with myriad new ways to make it even harder to vote. **The Department of Homeland Security has frozen critical election security programs. The Department of Justice is winding down defenses against foreign interference and domestic threats in our elections. And Congress is now considering blocking the funding that states use to provide ballot access.** Attacking the right to vote is yet another dangerous move toward fascism from Trump and his lackeys. As a check and balance on executive overreach, Congress must step up and defend our elections in 2026. [**Tell Congress: Protect the right to vote. subject: I wasn’t sure this country’s heart was big enough to love someone like me.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Hi Peter, it’s Congresswoman Sarah
McBride.

Right now, the GOP is using LGBTQ+ people as pawns. They’re not offering
solutions to make everyone's lives better. Instead, they’re busy launching
attacks — on our rights and yes, on me.

As the first openly trans member of Congress, I knew there would be
moments like this. But I didn’t run for Congress to debate which bathroom
I use or entertain cruelty from my Republican colleagues.

I ran to deliver for working families. To fight for paid leave. To protect
our freedoms. And I will never stop defending the LGBTQ+ community from
attacks, manufactured distractions, and the hostility too many of us
endure every day.

I won’t let the GOP’s pettiness and bullying derail my work. Has it been
easy? No. These fights never are. But I’ve never felt alone — because I
have people like you and Pramila Jayapal standing with me.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20250617-1?refcode=em20250617-5155&amount=3&refcode2=5155_420207_Y1ndWw&akid=5155%2E420207%2EY1ndWw ]If I can count on your support this Pride Month, split a donation of
$3 or whatever you can between my campaign and Pramila
Jayapal today. Every donation helps me defend the LGBTQ+ community and
keep up the fight for working families in Congress.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20250617-1?amount=3&refcode=em20250617-5155&refcode2=5155_420207_Y1ndWw&akid=5155%2E420207%2EY1ndWw ]Contribute

Growing up, I couldn’t imagine a future like mine. I wasn’t sure this
country’s heart was big enough to love someone like me.

Over the last decade, though, I’ve been able to bear witness to change
that once seemed so impossible to me as a kid that it was almost
incomprehensible. Because people believed it could. Because we fought for
it.

That’s what Pride means to me. It's a call to action and a reminder that
even in the face of hate, we have the power to fight back with love, with
truth, and with unshakable resolve.

Sarah

Colorado Newsline: Gov. Polis signs voting rights bill, shielding Colorado from federal backsliding [https://secure.everyaction.com/Z31SNww9Q0CZWIdx46cuSQ2?am=25.00&contactdata=2mrwkdctnO+9gnIg6lLBei3hEH/5Bcotc0WzoSXL9HxLX05326I43ki5hWQ5i1zgz73iF3pYdX6xyvMSIPmxU64wF9AdUKWuRh740gKg5go=]
Team,
Colorado's governor signed the Colorado Voting Rights Act into law yesterday, establishing various protections contained in the federal Voting Rights Act at the state level .
This new law prohibits election practices that limit the participation of people of color and other protected groups. It also includes protections for LGBTQ+ voters, expands multilingual ballot access, and requires accommodations for people with disabilities at residential facilities.
Most importantly, this law means Colorado does not need to rely on federal courts to enforce voting protections. The provisions of the law will apply to all state and municipal elections, and voters whose rights are violated under the act can take action along with civil rights groups -- a key right that is being dismantled at the federal level.
We need more states to take action like this, Team. Help us fight for a voting rights act in every state that doesn't have one with $25 or whatever you can today and make every vote count >> [https://secure.everyaction.com/pdjfDAEu4UCpXPQPEnrW-A2]

* **TOP NEWS**

"**With only 8% built, Texas quietly defunds state border wall program,** " Texas Tribune's**Zach Despart** and**Alejandro Serranos** - "Four years after Gov. **Greg Abbott** announced Texas would be the first state to build its own border wall, lawmakers have quietly stopped funding the project, leaving only scattered segments covering a small fraction of the border.

That decision, made in the waning hours of this year's legislative session, leaves the future of the state wall unclear. Just 8% of the 805 miles the state identified for construction is complete, which has cost taxpayers more than $3 billion to date. The Texas Tribune [reported last year](https://substack.com/redirect/cbcf06b7-7ecc-43ad-b113-6c0ce84ac819?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the wall is full of gaps that migrants and smugglers can easily walk around and mostly concentrated on sprawling ranches in rural areas, where illegal border crossings are less likely to occur.

State leaders suggested the federal government could pick up the effort. However, during President **Donald Trump 's** first term, when wall building was his top priority, his administration completed just 21 miles in Texas -- about a third of what the state was able to build over the past four years.

The Tribune reported [last year](https://substack.com/redirect/28029507-5386-4a5b-8a79-be66d0e8f03e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the state's wall program would take around 30 years and more than $20 billion to complete.

In early June, lawmakers finalized the state budget, approving $3.4 billion for ongoing border security efforts.

State Sen. **Joan Huffman** , the state's lead budget writer, confirmed to The Texas Tribune on Thursday that none of that money will go toward the wall. Instead, the funds will flow largely to the Department of Public Safety and Texas National Guard, the agencies tasked with apprehending migrants under Abbott's Operation Lone Star.

"It's not that we don't think it's an ongoing need to secure the border," said Huffman, R-Houston. "It should have always been a function of the federal government, in my opinion, and that wasn't really being done."

**Andrew Mahaleris** , Abbott's spokesman, said in a statement that the Trump administration's work to secure the southern border have allowed the state to adjust its own efforts. He did not specifically comment on the border wall program, but said the military and public safety departments would carry on their border-related missions.

"Texas will continue to maintain a robust presence with our federal partners to arrest, jail, and deport illegal immigrants," Mahaleris said.

Lt. Gov. **Dan Patrick** , who controls the Senate, did not respond to an interview request.

In the end, the Republicans who control the Legislature defunded the wall without any public debate.

The Texas Facilities Commission, the state agency in charge of building the wall, said as recently as January that its objective was to build at least 100 miles of wall by the end of 2026.

But it doesn't have the money to do so.

The wall program project manager in April reported that of the Legislature's $3 billion in funding from previous years, there was only enough left to complete 83 miles. The state has completed 65 miles. Work will continue on segments under construction but no new projects will begin, state officials said.

Texas Facilities Commission Executive Director **Mike Novak** did not respond to an interview request.

The Texas border wall has been a signature policy achievement touted by Abbott, who launched an expensive border crack down during the Democratic administration of President **Joe Biden**. He held multiple press events in recent years, touting construction of the 30-foot high wall -- which costs about $28 million per mile to build." TOP NEWS "With only 8% built, Texas quietly defunds state border wall program, " Texas Tribune'sZach Despart andAlejandro Serranos - "Four years after Gov. Greg Abbott announced Texas would be the first state to build its own border wall, lawmakers have quietly stopped funding the project, leaving only scattered segments covering a small fraction of the border. That decision, made in the waning hours of this year's legislative session, leaves the future of the state wall unclear. Just 8% of the 805 miles the state identified for construction is complete, which has cost taxpayers more than $3 billion to date. The Texas Tribune that the wall is full of gaps that migrants and smugglers can easily walk around and mostly concentrated on sprawling ranches in rural areas, where illegal border crossings are less likely to occur. State leaders suggested the federal government could pick up the effort. However, during President Donald Trump 's first term, when wall building was his top priority, his administration completed just 21 miles in Texas -- about a third of what the state was able to build over the past four years. The Tribune reported that the state's wall program would take around 30 years and more than $20 billion to complete. In early June, lawmakers finalized the state budget, approving $3.4 billion for ongoing border security efforts. State Sen. Joan Huffman , the state's lead budget writer, confirmed to The Texas Tribune on Thursday that none of that money will go toward the wall. Instead, the funds will flow largely to the Department of Public Safety and Texas National Guard, the agencies tasked with apprehending migrants under Abbott's Operation Lone Star. "It's not that we don't think it's an ongoing need to secure the border," said Huffman, R-Houston. "It should have always been a function of the federal government, in my opinion, and that wasn't really being done." Andrew Mahaleris , Abbott's spokesman, said in a statement that the Trump administration's work to secure the southern border have allowed the state to adjust its own efforts. He did not specifically comment on the border wall program, but said the military and public safety departments would carry on their border-related missions. "Texas will continue to maintain a robust presence with our federal partners to arrest, jail, and deport illegal immigrants," Mahaleris said. Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick , who controls the Senate, did not respond to an interview request. In the end, the Republicans who control the Legislature defunded the wall without any public debate. The Texas Facilities Commission, the state agency in charge of building the wall, said as recently as January that its objective was to build at least 100 miles of wall by the end of 2026. But it doesn't have the money to do so. The wall program project manager in April reported that of the Legislature's $3 billion in funding from previous years, there was only enough left to complete 83 miles. The state has completed 65 miles. Work will continue on segments under construction but no new projects will begin, state officials said. Texas Facilities Commission Executive Director Mike Novak did not respond to an interview request. The Texas border wall has been a signature policy achievement touted by Abbott, who launched an expensive border crack down during the Democratic administration of President Joe Biden. He held multiple press events in recent years, touting construction of the 30-foot high wall -- which costs about $28 million per mile to build." "**With only 8% built, Texas quietly defunds state border wall program,** " Texas Tribune's**Zach Despart** and**Alejandro Serranos** - "Four years after Gov. **Greg Abbott** announced Texas would be the first state to build its own border wall, lawmakers have quietly stopped funding the project, leaving only scattered segments covering a small fraction of the border.

That decision, made in the waning hours of this year's legislative session, leaves the future of the state wall unclear. Just 8% of the 805 miles the state identified for construction is complete, which has cost taxpayers more than $3 billion to date. The Texas Tribune [reported last year](https://substack.com/redirect/c226aec1-7f84-4fe7-a7dd-4a53fc7563ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the wall is full of gaps that migrants and smugglers can easily walk around and mostly concentrated on sprawling ranches in rural areas, where illegal border crossings are less likely to occur.

State leaders suggested the federal government could pick up the effort. However, during President **Donald Trump 's** first term, when wall building was his top priority, his administration completed just 21 miles in Texas -- about a third of what the state was able to build over the past four years.

The Tribune reported [last year](https://substack.com/redirect/af453683-c398-436d-9084-f19a92e33261?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the state's wall program would take around 30 years and more than $20 billion to complete.

In early June, lawmakers finalized the state budget, approving $3.4 billion for ongoing border security efforts.

State Sen. **Joan Huffman** , the state's lead budget writer, confirmed to The Texas Tribune on Thursday that none of that money will go toward the wall. Instead, the funds will flow largely to the Department of Public Safety and Texas National Guard, the agencies tasked with apprehending migrants under Abbott's Operation Lone Star.

"It's not that we don't think it's an ongoing need to secure the border," said Huffman, R-Houston. "It should have always been a function of the federal government, in my opinion, and that wasn't really being done."

**Andrew Mahaleris** , Abbott's spokesman, said in a statement that the Trump administration's work to secure the southern border have allowed the state to adjust its own efforts. He did not specifically comment on the border wall program, but said the military and public safety departments would carry on their border-related missions.

"Texas will continue to maintain a robust presence with our federal partners to arrest, jail, and deport illegal immigrants," Mahaleris said.

Lt. Gov. **Dan Patrick** , who controls the Senate, did not respond to an interview request.

In the end, the Republicans who control the Legislature defunded the wall without any public debate.

The Texas Facilities Commission, the state agency in charge of building the wall, said as recently as January that its objective was to build at least 100 miles of wall by the end of 2026.

But it doesn't have the money to do so.

The wall program project manager in April reported that of the Legislature's $3 billion in funding from previous years, there was only enough left to complete 83 miles. The state has completed 65 miles. Work will continue on segments under construction but no new projects will begin, state officials said.

Texas Facilities Commission Executive Director **Mike Novak** did not respond to an interview request.

The Texas border wall has been a signature policy achievement touted by Abbott, who launched an expensive border crack down during the Democratic administration of President **Joe Biden**. He held multiple press events in recent years, touting construction of the 30-foot high wall -- which costs about $28 million per mile to build." The wall program project manager in April reported that of the Legislature's $3 billion in funding from previous years, there was only enough left to complete 83 miles. The state has completed 65 miles. Work will continue on segments under construction but no new projects will begin, state officials said. Texas Facilities Commission Executive Director Mike Novak did not respond to an interview request. The Texas border wall has been a signature policy achievement touted by Abbott, who launched an expensive border crack down during the Democratic administration of President Joe Biden. He held multiple press events in recent years, touting construction of the 30-foot high wall -- which costs about $28 million per mile to build." * **TOP NEWS**

“**With only 8% built, Texas quietly defunds state border wall program,** ” Texas Tribune's**Zach Despart** and**Alejandro Serranos** – “Four years after Gov. **Greg Abbott** announced Texas would be the first state to build its own border wall, lawmakers have quietly stopped funding the project, leaving only scattered segments covering a small fraction of the border.

That decision, made in the waning hours of this year’s legislative session, leaves the future of the state wall unclear. Just 8% of the 805 miles the state identified for construction is complete, which has cost taxpayers more than $3 billion to date. The Texas Tribune [reported last year](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.taRaxrEkWqxIZl3CYy7RUxyhDaw8S8-J2PQlJO89hmZ7ueUipLglj_ZblTTRKVIbWH-05aCCLv6Z_Ee0ofV0H-7TDZgZr4yiOfyUoJ5_zQF8d-bO2X0YFaL9eLl0_LBFW_iggQKl1S9z3PwChWV-MW3lMaJt-YayxrYH4D_2cQi_MTv2i56XioegYYhIfEqinAafzNS6rqe9UzNF3ee1FL484rB5WClJYnUqbRcHI_AUizzdS1sC2Cz1qSatCmIULl2rZF2_42dm99hewgWJ7NjVwPuNY2dDmU32ux1sTJFRH3TDf1KRfSzQzPGp77LXXZr0SBXVcgnFX8UOLfGCX3Mxq_QFmmHvUWnCgzpshTXObhtw34tXjt-j8KlnJFYWJ27A1gorqhlYrmJVSF3XX7MMh7tSsbZxNeScok2IYxDQJu0ICPMdj0kzq5zARS_Ar1nUinKr609SbUPZ9mjctH3p9H4Zh-DDokIZdSz26Yt2bt-VJcD2geBPYVOjTopV/4hf/rdNE-FnsTOWwqpAF5S9veg/h10/h001.NgDwhDvHURQmu-QVzJLxlzcpgs-XME8igcifhNZKkxE) that the wall is full of gaps that migrants and smugglers can easily walk around and mostly concentrated on sprawling ranches in rural areas, where illegal border crossings are less likely to occur.

State leaders suggested the federal government could pick up the effort. However, during President **Donald Trump’s** first term, when wall building was his top priority, his administration completed just 21 miles in Texas — about a third of what the state was able to build over the past four years.

The Tribune reported [last year](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eCyDm7YZItPaA-BvJlf4tsCOy5MVrfFOkskQwqe1OdZtuOQVILJBNSP0PlfgtMU2e5Fk5S-d2gjmO7-P8O4EZ-e2k8jQ9pZoqbUbkJ7J21Fvp8Gd0KWKnYNkuWtNaOnB76tRvBANQVz41go3j7pc3BQHVIZQkgDHPTmSmOzmK-XIwQX8XvzsLgeODYwOjQGvW-W5hrPwfAp50LQZKY9zmhFZKbrGvQS6itErYFQL59UJl1xZklvyQGTN7IyV_Rm43i2HhxekOi5OgktrATUaAdjTSt6tVl9vLVKXMZo10zAjovYByVeM2pTviM8oCePCv8vDsCzJu3FhpQLVLHwcBMx6fAguTAMlMRJx54SqHJPjcyBzmJn9qh8JnfMKb9cPK__jj9KTYZAwPoeXvRczsIc_oACjzxz14YqIerzdc79I2lVXO-U1kl-JMrdU4KbNS07N7iacj7qW32RQf-1DDf9TNPla96-NzYf3r-2DaUvD/4hf/rdNE-FnsTOWwqpAF5S9veg/h12/h001.Wk3zAL3j1BZUlzvEmZ4KgfiH99LBhuxi3MxLIK9LWhg) that the state’s wall program would take around 30 years and more than $20 billion to complete.

In early June, lawmakers finalized the state budget, approving $3.4 billion for ongoing border security efforts.

State Sen. **Joan Huffman** , the state’s lead budget writer, confirmed to The Texas Tribune on Thursday that none of that money will go toward the wall. Instead, the funds will flow largely to the Department of Public Safety and Texas National Guard, the agencies tasked with apprehending migrants under Abbott’s Operation Lone Star.

“It’s not that we don’t think it’s an ongoing need to secure the border,” said Huffman, R-Houston. “It should have always been a function of the federal government, in my opinion, and that wasn’t really being done.”

**Andrew Mahaleris** , Abbott’s spokesman, said in a statement that the Trump administration’s work to secure the southern border have allowed the state to adjust its own efforts. He did not specifically comment on the border wall program, but said the military and public safety departments would carry on their border-related missions.

“Texas will continue to maintain a robust presence with our federal partners to arrest, jail, and deport illegal immigrants,” Mahaleris said.

Lt. Gov. **Dan Patrick** , who controls the Senate, did not respond to an interview request.

In the end, the Republicans who control the Legislature defunded the wall without any public debate.

The Texas Facilities Commission, the state agency in charge of building the wall, said as recently as January that its objective was to build at least 100 miles of wall by the end of 2026.

But it doesn’t have the money to do so.

The wall program project manager in April reported that of the Legislature’s $3 billion in funding from previous years, there was only enough left to complete 83 miles. The state has completed 65 miles. Work will continue on segments under construction but no new projects will begin, state officials said.

Texas Facilities Commission Executive Director **Mike Novak** did not respond to an interview request.

The Texas border wall has been a signature policy achievement touted by Abbott, who launched an expensive border crack down during the Democratic administration of President **Joe Biden**. He held multiple press events in recent years, touting construction of the 30-foot high wall — which costs about $28 million per mile to build." Greg Abbott announced Texas would be the first state to build its own border wall, lawmakers have quietly stopped funding the project, leaving only scattered segments covering a small fraction of the border. That decision, made in the waning hours of this year’s legislative session, leaves the future of the state wall unclear. Just 8% of the 805 miles the state identified for construction is complete, which has cost taxpayers more than $3 billion to date. The Texas Tribune that the wall is full of gaps that migrants and smugglers can easily walk around and mostly concentrated on sprawling ranches in rural areas, where illegal border crossings are less likely to occur. State leaders suggested the federal government could pick up the effort. However, during President Donald Trump’s first term, when wall building was his top priority, his administration completed just 21 miles in Texas — about a third of what the state was able to build over the past four years. » The Tribune reported that the state’s wall program would take around 30 years and more than $20 billion to complete. In early June, lawmakers finalized the state budget, approving $3.4 billion for ongoing border security efforts. » State Sen. Joan Huffman , the state’s lead budget writer, confirmed to The Texas Tribune on Thursday that none of that money will go toward the wall. Instead, the funds will flow largely to the Department of Public Safety and Texas National Guard, the agencies tasked with apprehending migrants under Abbott’s Operation Lone Star. “It’s not that we don’t think it’s an ongoing need to secure the border,” said Huffman, R-Houston. “It should have always been a function of the federal government, in my opinion, and that wasn’t really being done.” Andrew Mahaleris , Abbott’s spokesman, said in a statement that the Trump administration’s work to secure the southern border have allowed the state to adjust its own efforts. He did not specifically comment on the border wall program, but said the military and public safety departments would carry on their border-related missions. “Texas will continue to maintain a robust presence with our federal partners to arrest, jail, and deport illegal immigrants,” Mahaleris said. Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick , who controls the Senate, did not respond to an interview request. In the end, the Republicans who control the Legislature defunded the wall without any public debate. The Texas Facilities Commission, the state agency in charge of building the wall, said as recently as January that its objective was to build at least 100 miles of wall by the end of 2026. But it doesn’t have the money to do so. The wall program project manager in April reported that of the Legislature’s $3 billion in funding from previous years, there was only enough left to complete 83 miles. The state has completed 65 miles. Work will continue on segments under construction but no new projects will begin, state officials said. Texas Facilities Commission Executive Director Mike Novak did not respond to an interview request. The Texas border wall has been a signature policy achievement touted by Abbott, who launched an expensive border crack down during the Democratic administration of President Joe Biden. He held multiple press events in recent years, touting construction of the 30-foot high wall — which costs about $28 million per mile to build." | FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. **Cruelty Is the Point: How Playing into Trump’s Chaos Helps Him — and Hurts Us**
The Latino Vote Podcast Season 2025 Episode 18
| **As tanks roll into D.C. and protesters flood the streets of LA** , Chuck Rocha and Mike Madrid break down the chaos—**and the calculated cruelty driving it. **

With brutal honesty and a few **wrestling metaphors** (shoutout to Fritz Von Erich), the duo explores why **“Cruelty is the Point” isn’t just a phrase—it’s Trump's political strategy**. Blue-collar workers have **[seen nearly 2% real wage growth](https://substack.com/redirect/806252dc-6421-44f4-a035-757c0c4faa90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in Trump's first five months of his second term, representing the largest increase for any administration in nearly 60 years and a dramatic reversal from the 1.7% decline they experienced under Biden when inflation outpaced earnings.
* **Unprecedented Win For Trump 's Base:** Trump is the only president since Richard Nixon in 1969 to achieve positive wage growth for blue-collar workers in his first five months, having also recorded 1.3% growth in his first term. Every other administration has seen wage declines in comparable periods, with George H.W. Bush recording the worst drop at 3.0%.
* **Bessent Key To Policy Success:** Much credit for this economic turnaround belongs to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, whose strategic leadership has been instrumental in translating Trump's vision into tangible results. Bessent attributes the wage surge to falling inflation, Trump's emphasis on manufacturing, and efforts to remove illegal migrants from the workforce.
"Biden opened the border, and it was flooded," Bessent said in an appearance on the NY Post's 'Pod Force One' podcast. "And for working Americans, that's a disaster because it's pressure on their wages."
